_comment: Runtime config. Scoring weights live in scoring.json; map points live in map.json.

property._comment: Run `npm run setup -- --lat <lat> --lon <lon> --name "My place"` to fill this in. It writes config/config.local.json, which is gitignored and overrides this file, so your actual property never lands in version control.
property.name: My property

nws._comment: US only. Resolved once by setup from /points/{lat},{lon} and cached. Outside the US leave gridId null: wind, pressure and temperature still come from Open-Meteo, and only the NWS-sourced precipitation and sky cover are lost.
nws.userAgent: DeerHunter/1.0 (set a contact address here; NWS asks for one)

forecast._confidenceNote: Days 0-7 use real NWS forecast data (confidence: forecast). Days 8-14 use NWS where it still reaches, else climatology (confidence: outlook). Past day 14 it is rut curve + climate normals only (confidence: climatology).

drought._comment: Scales the food and water proximity weights by 1 + droughtBoost * severity. Updated automatically from the US Drought Monitor on every refresh when mode is 'auto', using the county FIPS that setup resolves. Severity is area-weighted across the county rather than taking the worst category present, so a corner in D3 does not read as uniformly extreme. Set mode to 'manual' to pin your own number: USDM is still fetched and logged each refresh, just not applied, which is the right choice if you know your own water better than a county-level map does.
drought._severityScale: 0 = no drought, 0.30 = D0 abnormally dry, 0.50 = D1 moderate, 0.75 = D2 severe, 0.90 = D3 extreme, 1.0 = D4 exceptional

alerts._thresholdNote: Deliberately uncalibrated. Run a season, look at the real score distribution on the Calendar tab, then set this to roughly the top 10-15% of slots. Too low and the alerts become noise.
alerts._windowNote: true = only alert on days with real NWS data behind them. Flip to false to also hear about climatology-only outlook days, which are much softer.
alerts._availableNote: true = only alert on days marked available on the Calendar tab. Useful once your PTO is planned; noisy before that.

discord._webhookNote: Intentionally empty in the tracked file. The real webhook lives in config/config.local.json (gitignored) or the DEERHUNTER_DISCORD_WEBHOOK environment variable. A webhook URL is a bearer credential: anyone holding it can post to the channel.

schedule._comment: America/New_York. refreshCron pulls weather and recomputes every slot in the season; alertCron checks thresholds and fires Discord.

server._hostNote: 0.0.0.0 so the Tailscale interface can reach it from your phone. No auth by design: single hunter, private tailnet.

map._layerNote: All four basemaps are keyless and were reachable on 2026-09-18. Esri caps out around z19 for this area; USGS Topo is the one with contour lines for terrain tagging.

scent._thresholdNote: Scent must blow at least this far off the bearing to a bedding or food point for the stand to read safe. 110-120 is the sane range; raise it to be stricter.
scent._radiusNote: Points farther than this from a stand are ignored in the scent check. Scent does travel farther, but past a few hundred yards it has diffused enough that stand choice is not what saves you.
scent._grazingNote: Below this angle the scent plume is a direct hit on the point; between here and safeAngleThresholdDeg it is a marginal graze. Scent cones spread roughly 30-45 degrees either side, so 60 is a deliberately conservative read of 'direct'.

climate._comment: Daily climate normals for the temperature-departure factor. setup computes these for your coordinates from 30 years of reanalysis. US users wanting NOAA station normals instead: npm run normals -- --station <GHCN id>

_seasonsNote: Define your own seasons here or on the Settings tab. Each has a date range, a weapon and a colour. Weapon is not cosmetic: it scales the scent-safety threshold, because an archer needs the deer inside 30 yards while a rifle hunter does not, so the same wind can be safe for gun and blown for bow. Seasons may overlap; where they do, the strictest open weapon governs. The tool scores the union of all enabled seasons. Dates are set by state and usually by county - check your own regs, these defaults are one NC zone.
